title: Informant-register subscriptions match through the NOW / EDT / prison-court-register branches, never an IR branch

oracle.activityBoundary: every callActivity argument and return value crosses oracle/lib/boundary.js
oracle.determinismCheck: the case was run twice at clockPinIso and the two document arrays compared

edits: subscriptions: three copies of the real nowSubscriptions[0], each given informantCode "ZZZ99" (deliberately matching nothing) and a fresh identity; the second additionally sets isNowSubscription true, the third isPrisonCourtRegisterSubscription true. isInformantRegisterSubscription stays true on all three, as in the captured data.

digests.convention: sha256 of the written file bytes — `sha256sum <file>` reproduces each value exactly

nodeEvidence.what: getSubscriptions has exactly four branches: matchCourtHouse (:19), matchProsecutor (:24), `subscription.isNowSubscription || subscription.isEDTSubscription` (:29), and `subscription.isPrisonCourtRegisterSubscription` (:39). There is no `isInformantRegisterSubscription` branch. The flag is used only as a pre-filter at InformantRegisterSubscriptions/index.js:28.
`matchCpsProsecuted` is declared and never called — a whole-repo grep for the identifier outside test files returns only this definition. Dead code.

``function matchVocabularyRules` (:114) opens with `if (subscription.applySubscriptionRules)` (:116) and, when that is falsy, skips the entire gate and reaches `return true` (:208-209). A NOW-flagged subscription with applySubscriptionRules false — which is every real informant-register subscription — matches unconditionally.
the only use of isInformantRegisterSubscription in this flow: a filter, applied before the matcher ever sees the list.

assertion: Three subscriptions are supplied, ALL with isInformantRegisterSubscription true and NONE with an informantCode or selectedCourtHouses that matches anything in the hearing (all three carry informantCode "ZZZ99"; the hearing gives TFL majorCreditorCode "CDE04" and TVL none at all). Assert EXACTLY: BOTH documents — TFL and TVL — have a `recipients` array of length 2 containing, in this order, "matched-via-now-branch" (isNowSubscription true) and "matched-via-prison-court-register-branch" (isPrisonCourtRegisterSubscription true); and NEITHER contains "not-matched-informant-register-only" (isInformantRegisterSubscription true and nothing else). Assert on BOTH documents, not just TFL: TVL has no major-creditor code at all, so the fact that it still collects both recipients proves these two branches never consult the authority. Two things are pinned. (1) Being an informant-register subscription is, by itself, not a reason to be matched; being a NOW or prison-court-register subscription is. (2) Those two branches are authority-blind, so one such subscription fans the register out to every authority in the hearing. A Java SubscriptionMatcher written from the field names — "this is the informant register flow, so match isInformantRegisterSubscription" — gets the opposite answer on all three subscriptions and MUST fail this test. D5 is priority-2: changing it needs the same SIT reference-data verification as D4 (design doc §13 Q8) plus a DEVIATIONS.md entry. Separately, and NOT assertable from any oracle case: matchCpsProsecuted (SubscriptionsService.js:56-59) is unreachable dead code. Do not port it. If a Java port contains a live cpsProsecuted matching branch, that is an unregistered behaviour change even though no golden case can catch it — cover it with a static check or a reviewer note, not with a test over this corpus.
